messages:
ashley: hey team, ACME reported weird embedding cache behavior — sometimes getting vectors with the wrong dimension back (expect 1024 but sometimes 1536). They noticed it only after we rolled the new quantized model variant. They provided a repro curl and a short log. can we triage? :grimacing:

joe: can you paste the exact curl + headers? is this reproducible from our side or only their environment?

ashley: paste incoming sample:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "x-tenant-id: acme" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"the quick brown fox"}'
```
response snippet they saw (trimmed):
```json
{"object":"embedding","embedding":[0.01, 0.02, ...], "model":"text-embedding-3-small"}  // length 1536 (unexpected)
```
They also said if they re-run a few times they sometimes get 1024.

mike: interesting. two quick hypotheses: (1) cache key doesn't include the quantization/profile/model_variant+dim so older cached vectors for a different variant leak into hits, (2) batch path is combining requests for multiple models/tenants and lookup is using a shared prefix.

joe: +1. i dug into the cache key code (emb_cache.lookup). current key format: `emb:sha1(input_text + model_name)` — i see no tenant or model_signature there. that's a red flag. seems like we assumed model_name was unique enough but model variants can have same base name.

ashley: they mentioned they rotate model config between `text-embedding-3-small` and `text-embedding-3-small-quant` via routing. maybe the base model_name in the payload is identical in some requests?

infra-bot: detected high cache hit variance for tenant=acme between 2026-05-03T14:02Z and 2026-05-03T14:08Z. 42% of hits returned vector lengths inconsistent with the expected `model_dim` reported by the serving runtime. trace_id=tr_9c7f2a

joe: that trace_id shows a mixed batch in the serving trace: requests from tenant `acme` and an internal test tenant were batched together. the batch lookup path did `multi_get` with keys generated from raw inputs, then we reassembled outputs into the batch order assuming key->vector_dim mapping consistent, but when a key collided (same sha1) we pulled a value produced by a different model variant.

mike: i can repro locally by crafting two inputs that intentionally collide on sha1 (short strings are easier) and invoking both with different `x-tenant-id` headers while our dev cache is using the shared prefix `emb_cache:default:`.

joe: repro steps I used:
```bash
# two clients (tenant a and tenant b) call the same input
curl -H "x-tenant-id: tenant-a" ... -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"collision-1"}'
curl -H "x-tenant-id: tenant-b" ... -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small-quant","input":"collision-1"}'
# inspect redis keys: keys emb:*collision-1*
redis-cli --scan --pattern 'emb:*collision-1*'
```
Then watch: one key created, reused by both tenants. stored vector dim corresponds to first writer.

ashley: oh — so this is a combined issue: (A) our cache key omitted tenant + model_signature + dim, (B) shared prefix + low TTL means a stale value from a different variant is considered valid.

mike: yes. second issue is TTL: we set default TTL to 24h. if tenant A writes a 1536 vector, tenant B later expects 1024 and hits the cache before regeneration, they get wrong length.

joe: proposed fixes:
- include `tenant_id` and `model_signature` (hash of model_name + quantization + model_dim) in the cache key
- add the model_dim as part of stored metadata so we validate dim on lookup and treat a mismatch as miss
- tighten TTL for new variant rollouts (short TTL during canary)
- add a gateway check to refuse/refresh cached value when dim mismatch is detected and keep a metric `emb.cache.dim_mismatch`

ashley: can we do a quick hotfix to stop cross-tenant reuse? maybe prefix keys with tenant id in the gateway as a config toggle while a proper patch is rolled?

mike: yes — easy toggle: `EMB_CACHE_STRICT_SCOPE=tenant` flips prefix from `emb_cache:default:` to `emb_cache:tenant:<tenant_id>:`. i can roll that as a config patch to gateway tonight and flip for prod.

joe: i'll prepare the code PR for the proper key change and the dim-check-on-lookup. tests will validate that a mismatch returns cache miss and logs. adding unit for multi-batch reorder to ensure mapping is correct.

ashley: reps to the customer: told them we see a cache keying bug and that we will enable a tenant-prefixed scope as an immediate mitigation and follow-up with a permanent fix. asked for any sample trace ids — provided tr_9c7f2a.

deploy-bot: scheduled deployment to canary cluster at 2026-05-03T23:45Z (patch: emb/gateway toggle EMB_CACHE_STRICT_SCOPE=tenant). change-id: D-2345

joe: after canary i will roll key-format patch to staging and run a load test with mixed-model batches to verify no accidental perf regressions.

mike: added a short-term alert: `emb.cache.dim_mismatch > 1` triggers page to infra oncall.

ashley: closing loop with ACME: i set expectation we'll have tenant-scoping live in canary tonight then full fix next week. they were okay with the plan. :thumbsup:

joe: thanks all — tracking in ENG ticket INF-9876. follow-ups: add metrics, add unit tests, perf run.

mike: leaving a note: long-term we should also consider hashing model binary fingerprint (weights checksum) into model_signature to avoid name-level ambiguity.

ashley: excellent. marking as resolved for now (mitigation in canary). will reopen if ACME sees recurrence. :white_check_mark:
